key_insight: FrozenLGP makes divide-and-conquer QAOA work on dense or highly connected graphs by freezing a small set of obstructing qubits and preserving their effect as bias terms.
engineering_relevance: It turns graph partitionability into an adaptive preprocessing step, enabling larger MaxCut problems to be mapped onto near-term quantum hardware with fewer entangling gates.
method: Use max-flow/minimum-vertex-cut to detect when standard graph partitioning fails.
Classically freeze the obstructing vertices’ spin assignments.
Fold removed interaction energies into neighboring linear bias terms in the Ising Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Across graphs up to 10,000 vertices, the method achieved 100% decomposition coverage versus 4.6% for the standard baseline on high-connectivity cases, while preserving MaxCut quality and improving noise robustness.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate cut computation and careful bias redistribution, so performance may be sensitive to how frozen assignments are chosen and implemented.
paper_title: Adaptive Qubit Freezing Enables Robust Graph Partitioning for Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
